findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Observed no certified food protection manager (CFPM) certification on site during today’s inspection. The PIC stated that he has his CFPM, but the certificate is stored at the Isles location where he just transferred from. Ensure CFPM certification is available for view by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee fail to hand wash before donning new gloves to begin a new task. Education was conducted regarding when to wash. Hands must be properly washed before donning a new pair of gloves to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed one sanitizer bucket on the prep line which measured 0ppm quaternary ammonia with a test strip. The sanitizer bucket was remade using the dispenser and measured 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure staff are frequently replacing the sanitizer buckets and measuring the concentration with a test strip.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed an employee drink stored with food for consumers in the standing coolers. The employee drink was moved to the bottom shelf during the inspection. Ensure staff use designated areas to store personal times to avoid cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
2nd Repeat Violation

PIC was unable to provide proof of food handler training certification for food employees at facility. Ensure valid food handler’s certifications are available for view for all employees by next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed foods stored in prep cooler 1, area to measure at temperatures between 60F and 70F. Manager stated that cooler is not operational, and that food is only stored in top area for approximately 1 hours at a time. No food is stored in bottom portion of cooler. Food items were placed on time as a control. Per PIC, food in cooler was placed there at 1130 AM. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Observed cutting boards mounted to surface of prep coolers to have deep knife gashes, making them no longer easy to clean and sanitize. Resurface existing cutting boards, or provide new cutting boards for prep coolers. 

4-501.12: Surfaces such as cutting blocks and boards that are subject to scratching and scoring shall be resurfaced if they can no longer be effectively cleaned and SANITIZED, or discarded if they are not capable of being resurfaced.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Observed unsealed wooden blocks used to prop up cooler in front of house area. Seal bare wood blocks, or remove from food service area. 

4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed the facility to be in operation with no sanitizer buckets or means of sanitizing surfaces as soiled during regular operation. Prepare and use sanitizer buckets or a means of sanitizing food contact surfaces during operation (such as sandwich board) and any other areas soiled by food. Sanitizer bucket was made during inspection, and tested at 200 ppm quaternary ammonia. 

4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
PIC was unable to provide proof of food handler training certification for food employees at facility. Provided proof of food handler certification for all food employees. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Observed facility to not have signed employee health and reporting agreements for employees. Provide a signed employee health and reporting agreement for all food employees at facility.

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

(B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Violation #10 has not been corrected by today, the follow up date set at the last inspection. Also, no communication has been received from the facility concerning the repairs. At this inspection the facility showed that they had a plumber in yesterday who was unable to fix the hand sinks so that hot water according to code is available. Upper management has been made aware of this along with some other maintenance issues at the facility. Maintain communication with the department. If corrections can not be completed by May10, 2022, yet progress is being made toward the repair, it may be acceptable to move the follow up date.

Repair all hand sinks (the kitchen and both restrooms) to provide water at the temperature required by code. 

5-202.12: (A) HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water of a temperature at least 100F through mixing valve. Pf (B) Steam mixing valve may not be used. (C) A self-closing, slow-closing, or metered faucet shall provide at least 15 seconds of flowing water. (D) An automatic sink shall be installed to manufacturer’s guidelines.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Temperature of hot water at all hand sinks in the facility is 59F by insertion of a probe thermometer into the water stream. Repair all hand sinks (the kitchen and both restrooms) to provide water at the temperature required by code. 

5-202.12: (A) HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water of a temperature at least 100F through mixing valve. Pf (B) Steam mixing valve may not be used. (C) A self-closing, slow-closing, or metered faucet shall provide at least 15 seconds of flowing water. (D) An automatic sink shall be installed to manufacturer’s guidelines.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Chemical sanitizer being used in the 3 part sink tests out to be 100 ppm of Quat sanitizer. The sink had been freshly made. Dish washer stated that they use 3 tablets in the sink. Tablets were added until the proper amount of sanitizer was registered on the test strip 200ppm. We recall that we used 5 tablets in the sink. Test the sink after dissolving sanitizer tablets and develop a habit of adding the proper number of tablets to reach the required concentration of sanitizer (between 200 ppm and 400 ppm according to test strips provided with the sanitizer tablets).
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Personal cleanliness
findings.comment:
Observed employee hair to be so long that it contacts counters when the employee turns around. Restrain hair so that it is not able to contact items that need protection from contamination. 

2-402.11: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall wear hair restraints designed and worn to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT; UTENSILS; and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. (B) Section is not applicable to FOOD EMPLOYEES who only serve BEVERAGES and wrapped or PACKAGED FOODS, hostesses, and wait staff if they present minimal RISK.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment: 2-102.11(B) (Pf) PIC is not a certified food manager. Provide proof of Food Service Sanitation Manager Certification.  Reference 2-102.11(B).
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(C)(10)(b) (Pf) PIC is not implementing knowledge concerning the relationship between food safety and equipment design, constructed, located, installed, operated, maintained and cleaned. Discussed the purpose and relationship between food safety and equipment. Reference 2-102.11(C)(10)(b).  Discussed the proper use of sandwich making table top. Keep food levels below the cold line of the prep table top and close when not in use. All employees state that the prpe table top is to be kept open per corporate policy. Food safety and public health guidelines are in place to help prevent food borne illness and should be implimened.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) The tea nozzle on the left dispenser is not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Foods in the prep table top closest to the cash register are between 49°F and 82°F . Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employees and person in charge. Inadequately held food was placed into a 4 hour rotation by time tag. These foods will be used or discarded by 5:30pm. The second prep table is currently holding temperature. The sandwich prep activity will be moved to that table until the other table can be repaired or begins to work after the air conditioning is repaired.  Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment: 4-204-112  (C) A thermometer is not provided in the 3 door cooler or the on use prep table. Cold/Hot holding equipment used for Time/Temperature Control for Safety food shall have at least one thermometer in an easily viewed location. Reference 4-204-112. Provide thermometers for all units holding TCS foods.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111  (Pf) Six house flies observed, live, in the area next to the walk in cooler . The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate flies, using proper pest control processes as needed. Keep doors closed so that the  entrance of insets and rodents is restricted. Reference 6-501.111.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on the back edge of the prep cooler top under the lid. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13. The prep table top was cleaned as it was being but into use.

A mechanical ventilation system of sufficient capacity shall be provided to keep rooms free of excessive heat, steam, vapors, obnoxious odors, smoke, and fumes. Reference 6-304.11.
